extra.message: user_id taken directly from request.POST['user_id'] is interpolated into a raw SQL string via % formatting and executed with User.objects.raw(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through the user_id form field.

hits_by_ip() builds a SQL statement with % string formatting using the ip value and column list, both derived from request.GET in admin_analytics (app/views/admin/views.py:90-98), then executes it via cursor.execute(cmd). Both the ip parameter and the column names are attacker-controlled, allowing SQL injection.

os.system("cp %s %s" % (full_file_name, bak_file_path)) is called with paths built from uploaded_file.name, which is attacker-controlled via the file upload at /upload. A malicious filename containing shell metacharacters (e.g. 'x; rm -rf /; cp') results in arbitrary OS command execution.

The download view concatenates request.GET['name'] directly onto BASE_DIR and opens the resulting path with file(path), returning its contents. An authenticated attacker can supply '../..' sequences to read arbitrary files on the server (e.g. /download?name=../../etc/passwd).

save_data() joins MEDIA_ROOT/data with uploaded_file.name without sanitization and writes the uploaded content there via default_storage.save. An attacker can supply a filename containing '../' to write arbitrary files outside the intended directory.

eval(classname) is executed on the raw value of the unauthenticated request.GET['class'] parameter. Any remote attacker can execute arbitrary Python code (e.g. __import__('os').system('...')) resulting in remote code execution.

eval(classname) is executed on the raw value of the unauthenticated request.GET['class'] parameter in api_id. Any remote attacker can execute arbitrary Python code, resulting in remote code execution.

reset_password() passes the base64-decoded value of the user-supplied POST parameter 'user' directly to pickle.loads(). Deserializing attacker-controlled pickle data allows arbitrary code execution on the server.

generate_token() builds the password-reset token as user_id + '-' + MD5(email) with no secret or randomness. Anyone who knows a victim's email and user_id can forge a valid reset token (is_valid_token at line 97 recomputes the same deterministic MD5) and take over the account.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: HttpResponseRedirect(path) uses the 'path' parameter taken verbatim from request.POST. An attacker can craft a login POST with path=https://evil.example to redirect users to an arbitrary external site after authentication, enabling phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: safe_name() returns mark_safe(self.first_name), and first_name is attacker-controlled via the signup and account-update forms. The value is rendered unescaped in template/layouts/shared/nav_loggedin.html:23 ('Welcome, {{ current_user.safe_name }}'), producing stored XSS executed in every logged-in page of the victim.

All admin views (admin_dashboard, admin_get_user, admin_delete_user, admin_update_user, admin_get_all_users, admin_analytics) are protected only by @user_is_authenticated; there is no is_admin check. Any authenticated non-admin user can delete arbitrary users (admin_delete_user), modify any account including passwords (admin_update_user), and view analytics data.

admin_update_user passes the entire request.POST dict (minus password fields) to User.objects.filter(...).update(**data). Combined with the missing is_admin check, any authenticated user can submit is_admin=True (or overwrite email/auth_token fields) to escalate privileges on any account.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: user_work_info_index fetches User.objects.get(id=user_id) using the user_id from the URL without verifying it belongs to the currently authenticated user. Any authenticated user can view any other user's work info, including their plaintext SSN, income and date of birth.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: user_message fetches Message.objects.get(pk=message_id) with no check that the message belongs to the current user. Any authenticated user can read (GET) or delete (DELETE) any other user's private messages by iterating message_id.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: user_pay deletes Pay.objects.get(id=pay_id) without verifying the record belongs to the authenticated user, and never checks request.user at all. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's direct-deposit/bank records.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: check_if_valid_token parses the Authorization token with the broken regex '(.*?)-(.*)' (re.search, '.' does not match newlines), while extrapolate_user (line 64) extracts the user id differently via re.split('[^0-9.]', ...). A token such as '1%0A2-<hash for user 2>' validates against user 2's hash but is then used to act as user 1, allowing API authentication bypass and user impersonation.

api_index serializes entire User model rows (including password MD5 hash and auth_token fields) to JSON and returns them to API clients. This exposes password hashes and session tokens of users, enabling offline cracking and session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Passwords are hashed with a single round of unsalted MD5 (hash_password, also used for comparison in authenticate() at line 107). MD5 is broken and unsalted hashes are trivially crackable with rainbow tables if the database is compromised.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: generate_token() creates the persistent session auth_token as MD5(email + random.randint(1,1000000)). The entropy is only ~20 bits and the MD5 input is predictable, so tokens can be brute-forced; the token is also stored in the database and never rotated, serving as a permanent bearer credential.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: The login handler returns distinct error messages: 'Email incorrect!' when the account does not exist and 'Password incorrect!' when it does. This allows an attacker to enumerate valid user email addresses (also reflected in the 'message' response header at line 62).

The auth_token session cookie is set without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite flags (both in the 'remember' branch at line 47 and here). The token is therefore accessible to JavaScript (amplifying the stored XSS via safe_name) and transmitted over plaintext HTTP.

password_reset_mailer sends every password-reset email (containing the account-reset link and token) to the hardcoded address 'vinai.rachakonda@contrastsecurity.com' instead of the requesting user. Whoever controls that mailbox can reset any user's password.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: DEBUG = True is enabled in the committed settings. In production this exposes detailed stack traces, settings values (including SECRET_KEY) and the Django debug toolbar to attackers.
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] disables Host header validation, enabling Host header poisoning attacks (e.g. cache poisoning and password-reset link poisoning).
The Django SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source control. Anyone with repo access can forge signed sessions/cookies and other signed data.

KEY = b'12345678910111212345678910111212' is a hardcoded AES key used by app/models/utils.py Encryption to encrypt SSNs and bank account numbers. A static, source-controlled key defeats the encryption of all sensitive fields.

ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT is hardcoded in settings.py. It is the only secret protecting API tokens (SHA1(salt:user_id) in app/views/api/users/views.py:60), so anyone with repo access can forge valid API tokens for any user id.
The MySQL database credentials ('root' / 'password') are hardcoded in docker_settings.py and committed to source control.

The seed command creates an admin account (admin@metacorp.com) with the hardcoded, well-known password 'admin1234' (plus several other users with hardcoded passwords). If the seeded database is deployed, these are default credentials allowing admin access. app/models/User/user_data.py:41 also hardcodes a reviewer account with password '12321' that is silently created for every new signup.

save_data reads the entire uploaded file into memory at once (uploaded_file.read() wrapped in ContentFile) instead of streaming with file.chunks(). Uploading a very large file exhausts server memory, enabling denial of service.
